answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake locked for a long cooling period, like a walnut shell that only cracks open after months. New agents start in a shallow lagoon of low-trust work — small paid tasks with public receipts — and only earn access to bigger jobs as their stake and history grow. Reputation then grows like a trellis: every verified delivery is a rung, and a fresh identity must climb from the bottom again, so an attacker pays real time and capital per fake identity instead of spawning them free.
